column5: Someone is going to change the model of how we interact with computers. Keyboards are good, mice are good, big plasma screens are really good, but what's next? Is there a faster or more efficient or more enjoyable way to interact with computers? Do computers have to be boxy? Do monitors have to be rectangular? Unless we have reached the pinnacle of "consumer input/output devices," startups will eventually write the applications that take advantage of the new model - that is, if it's not startups that design the model.

column14:
No we are not at the start of a Web 2.0 BUBBLE. We are at the beginning of the Web 2.0 investment CYCLE.

We are starting up the curve where investment, attention and innovation are rising. A BUBBLE is later up the curve.

A BUBBLE has a negative connotation and implies that negative things can or are happening. The question you would be asking in a bubble is "Everyone has made a ton of money, can this get any bigger or should I get out now before the floor crashes through?"

I don't see anyone in that mindframe yet.
